strings.name: Ha-Joon Chang
strings.role: Development economist and Research Professor of Economics at SOAS
strings.summary: Ha-Joon Chang is a South Korean development economist studying industrial policy, institutions and economic history. After a long teaching career at Cambridge, he joined SOAS University of London in 2022. His books for general readers contribute to debates on trade and capitalist institutions.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. The PhD year follows his own account of 1992; arguments for industrial protection are his views, not an academic consensus.
strings.influence.rationale: Studies industrial policy and development history, influencing debates on globalization and economic institutions through public writing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Holds a bachelor's degree from Seoul National University and master's and doctoral degrees from Cambridge; he dates his PhD to 1992 in his own account.
strings.facts.f2.label: Current roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Research Professor of Economics at SOAS and Co-Director of the Centre for Sustainable Structural Transformation.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Conditional industrial support
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advocates nurturing new industries in developing countries, with time limits and discipline for supported firms; he does not claim that every tariff generates growth.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Economics for general readers
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses accessible books to discuss economic schools, production and work, encouraging public understanding of economic policy choices.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Development-policy interview published
strings.timeline.t1.text: Finance & Development published an interview presenting his views on nurturing industries, trade and policy constraints.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Moved to SOAS
strings.timeline.t2.text: Joined the SOAS Department of Economics after teaching at Cambridge since 1990.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published an economics introduction
strings.timeline.t3.text: Economics: The User’s Guide appeared in the UK, introducing economics to general readers.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published a book on capitalism
strings.timeline.t4.text: 23 Things They Don’t Tell You About Capitalism appeared in the UK; the US edition followed in 2011.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Jointly received the Leontief Prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: Shared Tufts University's award for economic thought with Richard Nelson.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Book won the Myrdal Prize
strings.timeline.t6.text: Kicking Away the Ladder received the European Association for Evolutionary Political Economy's best monograph prize.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Published a study of development history
strings.timeline.t7.text: Kicking Away the Ladder examined development strategies from a historical perspective.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Began teaching at Cambridge
strings.timeline.t8.text: Started teaching economics at Cambridge; the start of his teaching career is distinct from the year his doctorate was awarded.
